## Caracol, Copán and Joya de Cerén: what connects the four countries?

A journey through [Belize](/belize/), [Honduras](/honduras/) and [El Salvador](/el-salvador/) offers three different perspectives on Central American history. [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) introduces the monumental architecture of an ancient Maya city. Copán in Honduras is especially compelling for its carved stone stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway. [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/) reveals everyday life in a settlement preserved under volcanic ash.

[Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) completes the four-country selection with nature rather than archaeology. On the particular itinerary, its days are devoted to cloud forest, volcanic scenery and Tortuguero. This is a valuable contrast, but it would be misleading to look for a fourth major ruins excursion there.

For this geography, we offer the [“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/). It also includes Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Panama. The four-country filter shows where these countries intersect with the “Culture and History” theme, **not a separate journey confined to those four countries**.

## Belize: Caracol as the beginning of the historical story

After arrival in Belize City, the itinerary continues to San Ignacio. Caracol is scheduled for the following day, including an ascent of Caana. The cultural significance of this day is the chance to explore an ancient Maya city in present-day Belize. The return route from Caracol passes through [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/), [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and [Rio On Pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/).

Allow enough time for the archaeological excursion itself: the nature stops are included in the same busy day. Independent exploration of additional temples or new sites is not included. Caracol is best understood alongside the later Maya monuments in Guatemala and Honduras rather than as an isolated attraction.

The next day brings a border crossing and a visit to Tikal in Guatemala, followed by cultural stops in Antigua and around Lake Atitlán. These places are important for understanding the broader sequence of Maya history, even though **Guatemala is not named in this four-country selection**. It cannot be excluded from the actual route when calculating journey times or documentation.

## Honduras: Copán and the art of stone writing

From Guatemala's Lake Atitlán, the route heads to Copán in Honduras. A separate day is allocated to the transfer; the following excursion focuses on the Copán ruins, carved stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway. UNESCO recognizes the outstanding cultural importance of the stairway and the sculpted monuments of the city center.

Copán should therefore not be seen as a repeat of Caracol. In Belize, visitors explore the monumental structures of an ancient city; in Copán, images of rulers, hieroglyphs and the sculptural detail of stone monuments command special attention. The visits address different aspects of Maya civilization.

An overland transfer to San Salvador follows the Copán excursion. This is a key logistical transition within the four-country historical story: sightseeing and crossing the border take place on the same day. An additional distant stop here should only be discussed after assessing actual driving times.

## El Salvador: life beyond the great ceremonial centers

The following day combines central San Salvador with [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/) and [San Andrés](/el-salvador/place/san-andres/). Joya de Cerén is protected as a UNESCO World Heritage site. Volcanic ash buried the settlement, preserving evidence of farming and everyday life before the arrival of Europeans.

The contrast with Copán is particularly revealing. In Honduras, the focus is monumental texts and ceremonial architecture; at Joya de Cerén, it is homes, work and the belongings of ordinary people. San Andrés adds another archaeological site from the region to the El Salvador section.

After this, the historical sequence is interrupted by a flight from San Salvador to Managua and the Nicaragua portion of the tour. Costa Rica begins later, after a separate flight from Managua to San José. The four-country filter therefore conceals a longer chain of transportation.

| Country | Main things to see |
|---|---|
| Belize | Caracol and Caana |
| Honduras | Copán, stelae and hieroglyphs |
| El Salvador | Joya de Cerén and San Andrés |
| Costa Rica | Nature rather than archaeology |

## How Costa Rica fits into the historical journey

The Costa Rica section includes [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), [El Tigre](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/), the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). Forest walks, a canopy tour, a volcanic park and a boat excursion on the canals are scheduled.

For travelers primarily interested in archaeology, this is an important trade-off: some of the overall 26 days are devoted to nature rather than further historic monuments. On the other hand, the route reveals the diverse geographical environments in which the region's cultures developed. If you want a tour exclusively devoted to Maya sites, it makes more sense to compare [cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/) emphasizing other combinations of countries.

## Practical considerations when visiting the monuments

The historic sites lie at different elevations and in different natural zones. At Caracol, account for the long outing and the combination of archaeology and nature stops; at Copán, allow enough time for the ruins before departure for San Salvador; at Joya de Cerén and San Andrés, check actual admission conditions for your dates. Opening times and access to individual areas must be confirmed against official rules before traveling, rather than a universal schedule for all of Central America.

Border crossings require a separate review of documents according to citizenship and the complete eight-country sequence. Re-entry and transit arrangements are critical for some travelers, so Ada Tours helps establish the list of crossings and flights before tickets are confirmed.

The stated itinerary lasts **26 days and 25 nights**, with excursions led by English-speaking guides, transfers and admission tickets according to the program. The final distribution of overnight stays and flight tickets still require confirmation; no departure dates or numerical price have been fixed. Listing a flight in the program must not be interpreted as a promise that its ticket is included.

## Frequently asked questions about the history of Belize, Honduras and El Salvador

### How are Caracol and Copán different?

Caracol in Belize is an ancient Maya city visited with an ascent of Caana. Copán in Honduras is particularly noted for its carved stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway. Both monuments appear in the full itinerary.

### Why is Joya de Cerén considered special?

Buildings and objects preserved under volcanic ash offer a rare view of everyday life in a pre-Columbian farming community. This differs from visiting monumental temples and palace complexes.

### Are archaeological excursions included in Costa Rica?

None are advertised on this tour. The Costa Rican days focus on natural areas, walking and the Tortuguero canals.

### Can we travel only through the four named countries?

The itinerary available in this selection covers eight countries. A shortened version, including its duration, logistics and cost, would need to be designed separately; a ready-made four-country product is not presented here.

## What nature experiences can these four countries offer?

If you are choosing a journey through [Belize](/belize/), [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/), [El Salvador](/el-salvador/) and [Honduras](/honduras/) for nature, check in advance **exactly where you will walk on trails, where you will travel by boat and how much time is available for observing animals**. The geography sounds varied, but the nature-focused content is unevenly distributed across the countries.

The current selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days”](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) also covers Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Panama. The four-country filter does not restrict the whole route to these countries: it identifies programs that include all four and in which nature is an important theme of the journey overall.

On this route, Belize stands out for upland forests and water, Costa Rica for ecosystems at different elevations and Caribbean lowlands. Honduras contributes an outstanding archaeological site in a green valley. El Salvador connects Central American history with the transition to the next stage. A nature park or volcano excursion in the latter two countries must not be treated as included simply because such attractions exist there. Routes without a theme filter are listed on the [Belize + Costa Rica + El Salvador + Honduras](/multi-country/belize_costa-rica_el-salvador_honduras/) page.

## Belize: a nature day away from the Caribbean coast

From [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/), the itinerary heads to Caracol and then through [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/). This part of Belize is characterized by pine trees, forest roads, granite streambeds and limestone formations. [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) adds a geological dimension, while [Rio On Pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/) offers a waterside stop with swimming when conditions permit.

The area differs noticeably from the tropical coast: air temperature and trail conditions vary with altitude and rainfall. Combining Caracol, the cave and the pools takes a full sightseeing day; adding a distant coastal site without changing the logistics would be impractical. Diving and visits to the barrier reef are not included on that day.

## Honduras: the Copán valley rather than a safari promise

Honduras is represented on our itinerary primarily by [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). After traveling from the Lake Atitlán region, the group spends a night near Copán, then visits the ancient Maya city, carved stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway the following day. The journey then continues to El Salvador.

The archaeological park stands in a valley with tropical vegetation, but **the day's main confirmed purpose is history and archaeology**, not a dedicated wildlife-watching excursion. UNESCO recognizes Copán as an important monument of the Classic Maya period. Visitors can see the relationship between terrain, ancient settlements and the cultural landscape without inventing a safari national park.

If you are attracted by Honduras's nature reserves or Caribbean islands, we can discuss a separate itinerary change. A visit to the reefs of Roatán, a walk in a reserve or a marine expedition is not automatically included by choosing this country combination. These require additional travel and a different time budget.

## El Salvador: a short stage between different geographies

In [San Salvador](/el-salvador/place/san-salvador/), the planned visits include the city center, Joya de Cerén and San Andrés. The transfer from Copán and the next flight make this stage predominantly cultural and logistical. El Salvador certainly has volcanic landscapes, but volcano visits are not stated in this itinerary.

The four-country combination thus suits travelers interested both in the nature days of Belize and Costa Rica and the rich historical context of Honduras and El Salvador. If the aim is the maximum number of nature hikes, it is more useful to discuss specific days in Monteverde and around Arenal than to assume equal levels of activity in every country.

## Costa Rica: from cloud forest to the Tortuguero canals

The Costa Rican part includes several distinct natural settings. In [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), travelers walk through cloud forest and then take a canopy tour. Resplendent quetzals and other birds occur in suitable habitat, but the species actually seen depend on season and luck.

At [El Tigre Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/), an approximately three-hour trail is planned, of moderate to demanding difficulty, with rocky stretches and water crossings. Then comes [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/): hot springs, hanging bridges and paths across old lava fields. The current itinerary does not include climbing the active volcanic cone.

After the mountain and forest days, the route reaches [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), with part of the journey by boat along rivers and canals. A dawn excursion offers chances to observe birds, reptiles and rainforest life by the water. Visits to turtle colonies and encounters with particular animals depend on natural conditions, so the tour offers no such guarantees.

## Why the border sequence matters more than distances on a map

On a map, the four selected countries form an attractive combination, but **the real 26-day itinerary does not travel directly from Belize to Honduras**. Guatemala comes between them: Tikal, Antigua, Pacaya and Atitlán. Honduras and El Salvador follow, then Nicaragua; Costa Rica begins after a flight from Managua. Counting days only between the four filter names would underestimate hotel nights, domestic flights and border crossings.

Honduras and El Salvador belong to the CA-4 group together with Guatemala and Nicaragua. These are regional arrangements, not a universal tourist visa covering all passports or every Central American country. Belize and Costa Rica have their own rules. **For Russian citizens**, current admission and transit conditions must be checked for each land crossing, flight and period of stay. Travelers with other citizenships have different requirements. Ada Tours helps organize these checks around the entire itinerary without guaranteeing decisions by border authorities.

## Weather, clothing and physical effort

The journey covers several climatic conditions. Belize's pine-covered hills, Honduras's green valleys, El Salvador's city stops and Costa Rica's humid forests require different clothing even in the same month. Rain is possible in Tortuguero regardless of a dry season elsewhere in Central America, while Monteverde's damp, cool conditions differ from the heat of the lowlands.

A practical kit includes quick-drying clothes, a raincoat, comfortable trainers or hiking boots, a lightweight warm layer and protection for belongings against water. Assess your fitness for El Tigre and other active walks in advance; comfortable transfers do not eliminate exertion on the trails.

Belize uses the Belize dollar, Honduras the lempira, Costa Rica the colón and El Salvador the US dollar for payments. Currencies and card acceptance vary by stop. Before departure, check whether Russian or other foreign bank cards work at the actual locations, exchange conditions and the amount of backup cash needed. There is no fixed exchange rate or guaranteed acceptance of any particular card for the entire journey.

## Choosing an itinerary without confusing nature with a country's name

For a nature-focused trip featuring the four named countries, review the sequence of specific activities: the highlands of Belize, Monteverde, El Tigre, Arenal and Tortuguero. Then decide how well the cultural days in Copán and San Salvador fit your interests. They are worthwhile in their own right, but the nature theme is less prominent there.

If volcanoes and mountain lakes interest you more, compare the nearby [combination with Guatemala](/multi-country/belize_costa-rica_el-salvador_guatemala/interests/nature/). For other countries and formats, explore [multi-country tours](/multi-country/) or [nature-focused journeys](/interests/nature/). Shortening the eight-country program to four countries should be considered as a custom change with days recalculated, rather than an existing package without a confirmed description.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador and Honduras

### Can we visit the reefs of Roatán in Honduras on this itinerary?

Our 26-day route includes Copán, not Roatán. A marine section in Honduras would require extra time and a revised itinerary; neither its inclusion nor its price is confirmed in advance.

### Is this combination suitable for wildlife watching?

There are opportunities primarily in Costa Rican forests and the Tortuguero canals, as well as Belize's natural areas. Specific species and sightings cannot be guaranteed. Copán and the archaeological sites of El Salvador should not be described as a full wildlife-watching program.

### How many countries does the selected tour actually cover?

The [Ada Tours itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) lasts 26 days and covers eight countries. The four countries in this page title are a geographical and thematic filter; they do not shorten the existing route.

### Can the more difficult walks be removed?

That is a matter for custom adaptation. In particular, discuss the El Tigre trail with its rocks and water crossings in advance. Removing an activity may affect other transfers and tour conditions, so a substitution cannot be assumed to be included automatically.

### Do all four countries have one shared border regime?

No. CA-4 covers Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua, while Belize and Costa Rica have separate rules. Entry and transit documents must be checked for each citizenship and itinerary.

## A nature route through Belize, Honduras, El Salvador and Costa Rica

The [Belize](/belize/) + [Honduras](/honduras/) + [El Salvador](/el-salvador/) + [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) selection is grouped under the “Wildlife” interest, but **wildlife watching occupies only part of the entire journey**. Belize provides walks through forested areas and stops beside rivers, while Honduras and El Salvador focus mainly on historic monuments. In Costa Rica, the itinerary moves into cloud forests and waterways, with specific activities devoted to nature and observing animals.

We offer a [26-day tour through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), also visiting Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Panama. The selected four are a thematic filter applied to the main countries of the complete tour, so many cultural and transport days lie between the nature stops in Belize and Costa Rica. This catalogue does not promise a separate, continuous four-country safari.

## What Belize actually offers: Mountain Pine Ridge and Rio On

The Belize section begins with arrival via Belize City and transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/). The next day travelers visit Caracol, then pass through [Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/), [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and the natural [Rio On Pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/). Swimming and relaxation are planned at the pools.

The nature theme here is landscape diversity: pine woods, the cave's stone arches, a river and natural rock pools. This is an appealing stop for visitors interested in Belize's nature alongside archaeology. **No special excursion to search for birds, wild cats or other particular animal species is advertised here.** Even when a region supports many species, their presence does not guarantee a sighting.

Immediately after the Belize day, the itinerary crosses into Guatemala. It proceeds to Tikal and other areas of Guatemala before reaching Honduras and El Salvador. The Belize nature section cannot simply be extended by several days while assuming the dates of the full journey remain unchanged.

## Why the itinerary has no safari in Honduras or El Salvador

The Honduras stop centers on Copán, a Maya archaeological site. The planned visits include ruins, carved stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway, followed by a transfer to San Salvador. The following day in [El Salvador](/el-salvador/) includes a city tour and visits to [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/) and [San Andrés](/el-salvador/place/san-andres/).

These days have real value for discovering the region's history, but should not be marketed as wildlife watching. The confirmed itinerary has no separate nature excursion in Honduras or El Salvador. Travelers hoping to spend every day observing birds and mammals should assess how much of the program is cultural.

Unlike the combination with Guatemala, whose selected four countries include forested [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), this filter includes Honduras and Copán instead. That changes the thematic emphasis of the four selected countries, **even though the underlying eight-country tour remains exactly the same**.

## Costa Rica: Monteverde and Tortuguero at the heart of wildlife watching

In [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), a morning walk through the cloud forest reserve is planned. You may see a quetzal on the walk, but neither a particular species nor the moment it appears can be reliably guaranteed. A canopy tour follows in the afternoon; it is an active experience rather than a substitute for a quiet wildlife-watching walk.

The program then visits [El Tigre Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/) and [Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). At El Tigre, expect around three hours on foot over rocky stretches and river crossings; near Arenal, hanging bridges and a walk through the volcanic park are planned. These days immerse travelers in Costa Rica's landscapes, but none of them promises sightings of particular animal species.

The most specifically scheduled **wildlife-watching experience** takes place at dawn in [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/): a boat trip along the national park's canals. Costa Rica's conservation authority SINAC describes these waterways as habitats for water birds, reptiles and other fauna. Sightings still depend on weather, boat movements and animal behavior. It helps to decide what interests you most: photographing birds, quietly viewing the swamp forest from the water or exploring the national park more broadly.

## How the type of outing, time of day and conditions differ

| Stop | Format on the tour |
|---|---|
| Mountain Pine Ridge | Forest and nature stops |
| Copán | Historical excursion |
| Joya de Cerén | Archaeological excursion |
| Monteverde | Morning forest walk |
| Tortuguero | Dawn boat excursion |

The mornings in Monteverde and the dawn outing in Tortuguero are intended for nature, but take place in different landscapes. Monteverde is a mountain cloud forest; Tortuguero is a humid Caribbean lowland of rivers and canals. Clothing, footwear and rain protection may therefore differ. Stable footwear is important for the walking sections; protect your camera and phone from water on the boat.

Tortuguero is also known for marine turtles and regulated seasonal observation. However, **a beach visit to watch turtle nesting is not included in the current 26-day tour**. The scheduled excursion is on the canals. Anyone considering a separate turtle-watching experience should check the season, access arrangements and permitted visiting formats, then see whether it fits the calendar of the full trip.

## Planning flights and time for nature

Between Belize and Costa Rica come sections in Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua. After San Salvador, the route includes a flight to Managua and later a flight from Managua to San José. In Costa Rica, the tour continues with road transfers and a boat trip to Tortuguero. **The time between nature stops cannot be estimated from the straight-line distance between Belize and Costa Rica.**

No fixed dates are specified for the 26-day itinerary. To travel during the nature season that interests you, Ada Tours helps coordinate the calendar, movement between countries and park access. Neither rain-free weather nor a sighting of a particular animal can be guaranteed. Entry documents and flights are checked for all eight countries and each traveler's citizenship.

The excursions on this tour are conducted in English. International and domestic air tickets appear among the exclusions, while the distribution of hotel nights and commercial quotation require agreement. If your priority is to maximize days in nature without long cultural stops, compare [wildlife-watching tours](/interests/wildlife/) with the specific [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife watching

### In which of the four countries are observations actually planned?

The main wildlife opportunities are in Costa Rica: the Monteverde cloud forest walk and the Tortuguero canal excursion. Belize provides nature stops, while Honduras and El Salvador focus on archaeology.

### Will we see jaguars, quetzals or sea turtles?

The itinerary explicitly mentions a possible quetzal sighting in Monteverde, with no guarantee. It does not advertise a jaguar safari or a separate turtle-nesting excursion. Wild animal encounters depend on natural conditions.

### Can we shorten the cultural part to spend more time in nature?

A custom change can be discussed. However, the confirmed product lasts 26 days and covers eight countries; shortening it requires new calculations for flights, road transfers, nights and available nature excursions.

### Why is wildlife watching concentrated in Costa Rica?

Costa Rica includes a Monteverde cloud forest walk and a dawn excursion to observe the inhabitants of the Tortuguero canals. Hanging bridges, El Tigre waterfalls and the Arenal volcanic park offer scenery linked to the [Nature theme](/interests/nature/). The other three countries play different roles on this itinerary, so the “Wildlife” label applies to the tour as a whole.

## Mexico, Belize, El Salvador and Costa Rica: what itinerary is available?

**Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} covering all four countries.** At present, this is [“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days”](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/). The trip also includes Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama. The selection indicates that the four named countries appear on the main itinerary; it does not mean the journey is restricted to them.

The route proceeds from [Mexico](/mexico/) through [Belize](/belize/) and other countries of the region to [El Salvador](/el-salvador/), then through Nicaragua to [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and Panama. Its strength lies in the variety of historic and natural attractions; its main organizational challenge is the series of flights and border crossings between countries with their own immigration rules.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

If you want only these four countries, the route needs to be designed separately. There are no direct overland connections between every pair, so deleting the intermediate countries on paper is easier than doing so in practice.

## Starting in Mexico: Mexico City, Yucatán and entry arrangements

The opening days of the current itinerary take place in Mexico. The first stops are [Mexico City and its surroundings](/mexico/place/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/), the historic center, the Anthropology Museum and [Teotihuacán](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/). A flight to [Mérida](/mexico/place/merida/) then follows, along with a visit to [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) and time in [Cancún](/mexico/place/cancun/) before flying to Belize.

This order matters for climate and luggage: Mexico City is at high elevation, while Yucatán is considerably hotter. Clothes for a cool Mexico City evening and light clothing for humid coastal heat may both be needed on the same trip.

**Entry into Mexico for Russian citizens depends on the mode of arrival.** Mexico's National Migration Institute describes the SAE electronic authorization for Russian tourists arriving by air: it must be obtained before departure, has its own validity period and applies to a single entry. Land and sea entries are subject to different conditions; an authorization for flying must not be assumed valid at a land border. Before buying tickets, check the current rules for your citizenship, passport type and connecting airport.

## Belize: from the airport to Caracol and the next border

Our tour includes a **flight from Cancún to Belize City**, followed by a vehicle transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/). The next day, travelers visit [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), the Mountain Pine Ridge forest area, Rio Frio Cave and [Rio On Pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/). The route then crosses from Belize into Guatemala on the way to Tikal.

This means the Mexico–Belize stage is **not organized around a land crossing at Chetumal**. Replacing the flight with a road journey would require recalculating time, entry point, transportation and overnight stays, rather than simply changing a ticket.

Belize is not part of CA-4. Entry into Belize and the following entry into Guatemala must be checked separately. Even where a tourist is visa-exempt, passport requirements and proof of travel purpose still apply.

## El Salvador and Costa Rica: linked by theme but not by a shared border

In El Salvador, the itinerary includes [San Salvador](/el-salvador/place/san-salvador/), the [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/) archaeological complex and San Andrés. A flight from San Salvador to Managua follows, along with several days in Nicaragua. Only after that do travelers fly to San José and travel on to Costa Rica.

The Costa Rican section focuses on nature: [Monteverde cloud forest](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), walks to El Tigre Waterfalls, the [Arenal Volcano area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and the [Tortuguero canals](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). This is a substantial nature-focused part of the journey, not a brief stop between flights.

El Salvador belongs to CA-4 along with Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. Permitted days of stay for foreign tourists in this group may be counted jointly, and a subsequent entry into a CA-4 country does not automatically reset the allowance. **Costa Rica and Belize are not part of CA-4** and have separate rules. Transit through a third country on a flight from El Salvador to Costa Rica should also be checked.

## Money: four countries and different currencies

| Country | Main currency |
|---|---|
| Mexico | Mexican peso, MXN |
| Belize | Belize dollar, BZD |
| El Salvador | US dollar, USD |
| Costa Rica | Costa Rican colón, CRC |

The Central Bank of Belize maintains a fixed rate of **2 BZD to 1 USD**. This helps when comparing prices but does not guarantee that every shop will give change in the desired currency or accept a damaged banknote. Small denominations of local money are useful for everyday expenses.

On a long journey, separate your main budget from reserves for borders, meals outside the program, tips and personal purchases. Holders of cards issued by Russian banks should check whether they actually work abroad and have an independent payment method. US-dollar cash does not substitute for local currency everywhere.

## Flights, seasons and the budget for a 26-day itinerary

### Can I restrict the journey to Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador and Mexico?

### Do El Salvador and Costa Rica share a border?

No. Nicaragua lies between them. On the specific 26-day itinerary, travelers fly from El Salvador to Managua, explore Nicaragua and later fly from Managua to Costa Rica.

### Is one Central American visa required?

There is no universal authorization covering all eight countries. CA-4 regional arrangements concern Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua; Mexico, Belize and Costa Rica apply their own requirements. Check these according to citizenship and means of crossing the border.

The main product is packed with archaeological excursions, walks and nature routes. Prioritizing a beach holiday would require a different allocation of days. The [combined-journeys catalogue](/multi-country/) is a starting point when choosing destinations.
